movement_source: row 'CET1 capital ratio (Level 2 Group)', column 30 Sep 24 column -> column 30 Sep 25 column
headline: NAB's APRA Level 2 (Group) CET1 ratio fell 65 bps over FY25, from 12.35% at 30 Sep 2024 to 11.70% at 30 Sep 2025 (results book KPI table and capital ratios table). The bank attributes the reduction to lending volume growth, increased long-term investment in the business, and the completion of the on-market share buy-back, which it quantifies at -15 bps for the $0.6 billion of shares bought back in FY25. NAB does not publish a full-year (Sep 24 to Sep 25) capital walk; the only walk disclosed is the half-on-half (Mar 25 to Sep 25) movement, which is a different comparison. Pro forma Group CET1 of 11.81% reflects the sale of the remaining 20% stake in MLC Life (completed 31 Oct 2025).

drivers.narrative: The bank states the impact of $0.6 billion of shares bought back in FY25 was -15 bps. The buy-back of $3 billion announced 15 Aug 2023 (increased 2 May 2024) completed 12 Mar 2025; 16,572,039 shares ($0.6bn or 0.15% of CET1 capital) were bought back in the Sep 2025 full year.

The bank names lending volume growth as a key driver of the FY25 CET1 reduction but does not quantify its bps impact for the full-year comparison. Credit RWA rose from $350.9bn (Sep 24) to $375.0bn (Sep 25); the half-on-half walk attributes -45 bps to credit RWA over Mar-Sep 25.

drivers.bank_label: Increased long term investment in the business
drivers.narrative: The bank cites increased long-term investment in the business as a key driver of the FY25 CET1 reduction but does not quantify its bps impact for the full-year comparison. Investment spend rose to $1.8bn in FY25 from $1.6bn in FY24.

limitations: NAB does not publish a full-year (Sep 24 to Sep 25) capital walk. The only walk disclosed is the half-on-half (Mar 25 to Sep 25) movement: 12.01% +0.82 (cash earnings) -0.61 (dividend) -0.45 (credit RWA) +0.01 (other RWA) -0.08 (other) = 11.70%. These bars are a DIFFERENT comparison and were NOT used as this period's driver contributions.

Only the buy-back (-15 bps) is quantified for the full-year comparison. The remaining -50 bps of the -65 bps movement is unquantified by the bank (lending volume growth and increased long-term investment are stated qualitatively).
The half-on-half walk's credit RWA bar (-45 bps) is context only; the full-year credit RWA contribution is not separately quantified.
Pro forma CET1 of 11.81% reflects the MLC Life sale which completed after the balance date (31 Oct 2025); it is a different measure from the reported 11.70%.
No published walk covers FY25 vs FY24: the bank's walk for this metric describes another comparison, so the driver split is not walk-verified for this comparison. Confidence is capped at 85.

Group CET1 ratio of 11.70%, down (65 bps) from September 2024. Key drivers of the reduction include lending volume growth, increased long term investment in the business and the impact of $0.6 billion of shares bought back in FY25 (-15 bps)
Proforma Group CET1 ratio of 11.81% reflecting the sale of the Group's remaining 20% stake in MLC Life.

On 12 March 2025, the Group completed the on-market buyback that was announced on 15 August 2023 and subsequently increased on 2 May 2024 to $3 billion. Through this buy-back, the Group has bought back and cancelled 87,824,707 ordinary shares, including 16,572,039 ordinary shares ($0.6 billion or 0.15% of CET1 capital) in the September 2025 full year.
